finding.text: Asks 3–7 are not in this diff (requirements 3–7): `public/framework/ai/2026-10-12/` and `2026-10-13/` are still on disk, and there is no tree decision, no readme pattern, no owner note and no card report. `ai/readme.md` line 3 still says "one folder per day". This diff is step 2 of 7, so the task cannot land on it.

`ai/page.js:115` sends every `/framework/ai/<day>/<slug>/` without its own page.js to `StoreFolder.lookup`, and drops the `AITask` fallback. The 2026-10-12 tasks still sit in the flat folder until step 3, so if this merges first their pages depend on the `tasks` query index finding them. On the static site that index does not exist, so they show "not in the index". Either merge only together with step 3, or keep `AITask` when the old folder still exists.

Step 2 asked for proof "on a private Servex from a worktree"; it was proved with stub calls instead (`Start.scaffold` in a scratch repo, `TaskDirs.test.mjs`). The `decision` line in task.jsonl records why and names the alternative, so this is acceptable, but it is not what the brief said.

Small code leftovers: `Start.js` declares `day` and never uses it. `crawl.mjs:352` has its `;` inside the trailing comment. `CardAnswer.js` keeps an empty `{ … }` block from the old inner loop. `merge.mjs` repeats `TaskDirs.locate` inline instead of calling it (law 6, one of everything).
`TaskDirs.refuse` only guards `append.mjs`. A script that calls `fs.mkdirSync` directly is caught only by the `--census` regex, which is a heuristic. The audit doc says so, and that is honest.
